verdict: 2026-07-25 09:23 PDT — The slice-first Workflow pipeline is the right overall architecture, but I would not ship this as the reusable harness future lenses copy. The source binding rejects artifacts the planner permits, the supposedly deterministic adjudication still requires semantic AI judgment, and execution lifecycle state remains split across prose-only structures. I would retain Workflow, Git, and Draft-7—the repo has no conventional dependency manifest—but drive them from versioned source, claim/evidence, and run-state contracts.

findings.title: Source identity has two incompatible contracts
findings.claim: The planner can produce and approve dirty-tree plans, but the engine categorically refuses them and defers support. That contradicts AC2 and creates an approved artifact that the hand-off cannot execute. It also splits one source-identity invariant into revision-based clean handling and a future dirty-tree mechanism, with bespoke hashing logic around the split.
findings.alternative: Extend plan-schema v1 now with one canonical `source.contentFingerprint`, computed over the audited tracked-file set excluding `reviews/**` for both clean and dirty plans. Recompute and compare that same digest at execution; retain `revision` and `dirty` as provenance rather than alternate identity mechanisms.
findings.win: Eliminates the dirty-plan rejection path and clean/dirty branching, centralizes source identity in one field and one comparison, and makes every plan the compiler approves executable by the engine.

findings.title: The deterministic adjudicator has no deterministic inputs
findings.claim: The finder emits an unrestricted prose `claim`; the evidence record leaves `controlFlow` and `reachableOutcomes` as prose; and the alleged decision table merely says to promote when those fields “corroborate the claim's specific mechanism.” No deterministic operation can perform that semantic comparison. The suggested adjudicator team therefore reintroduces model judgment—and the echo-chamber risk—at the stage intended to remove it.
findings.alternative: Make finder claims and verifier observations discriminated unions. For this lens, encode a small claim taxonomy and decisive facts such as construct-present, handler action, error propagation, degraded continuation, and mechanical-check result. Use one declarative claim-class × evidence-facts promote/refute table; keep prose only as explanatory material.
findings.win: Removes the adjudicator-agent/team and its error path, makes promotion mechanically reproducible, and preserves claim blindness while giving every future lens an explicit extension point.

findings.title: Manifest and ledger are postulated, not modeled as one execution contract
findings.claim: The run manifest is only a six-field prose record and validates cardinality but not the AC4 estimated-cost equality. Execution state is then reconstructed after the run in a separate report ledger containing only `executed` and `omitted`; `planned` and `failed` are deliberately absent. Consequently Workflow must hand-roll lifecycle transitions and failure accounting, while a failed run leaves no ledger that mechanically distinguishes it from a run that never began. This is the cross-cutting pattern later lenses would inherit.
findings.alternative: Use one versioned run artifact initialized before spawning: full row identity, child run records, approved estimated cost, model provenance, and `planned`/`executed`/`omitted`/`failed` state with verified-finding count. Validate cardinality, cost, and model separation before launch; transition that artifact during execution; derive the success report only when no row is failed.
findings.win: Centralizes manifest, failure, provenance, and coverage invariants; eliminates post-hoc ledger reconstruction; makes AC4, AC6, and AC7 mechanically checkable from one artifact; and gives failures an observable record without publishing a partial report.
